note: Where the outline is wrong and a human is right. A 50 m coastline rounded to three decimals cannot resolve a border that runs three kilometres from a village, so a handful of places need saying out loud. Keyed by place id, and every entry must carry a reason — an override with no reason is indistinguishable from a typo. Two kinds of entry live here and they are not the same thing: an outline too coarse to see an enclave, and ground whose sovereignty is disputed. The second kind says which filing this atlas follows and why, because a records map that pretends the question is settled is lying about where to write.

vitaljina.why: Croatia's southernmost settlement, in Konavle. The Montenegrin border is 3 km away and the rounded outline puts the point on the wrong side of it.

melilla.why: A Spanish city on the North African coast since 1497, and one of the two places in Europe where the outline file and the filing cabinet genuinely disagree. Natural Earth's 50 m coastline draws the Moroccan shore straight through it. Its civil registry is Spanish and its records are in the Spanish system, which is what this map is for.

carriacou-and-petite-martinique.why: A dependency of Grenada, and the outline puts it with the Saint Vincent Grenadines because that is the island chain it sits in. Its registers are Grenadian.

crimea.why: Russian-administered since 2014; Natural Earth draws the de facto line. Filed here as Ukraine, which is the internationally recognised sovereignty and — the reason that matters for this atlas — the filing under which the historical registers were catalogued and digitised. The ground is disputed; where the paper was indexed is not.

sevastopol-city.why: As Crimea, of which it is the separately administered city. Same dispute, same filing, same reason.

borojevici.why: Filed as BA until 16 Oct 2026. Corrected because its registers sit in FamilySearch collections filed under Croatia, and the same-name GeoNames row 0.0 km from the point, «Borojevići», is in HR. The point is within 25 km of the border, which the rounded outline cannot resolve.
